item.title: Jellyfish became a threat to France's Gravelines plant after clogging cooling systems
item.description: In a striking environmental incident, a massive jellyfish swarm has compelled the shutdown of reactors at France's Gravelines nuclear plant. The clogged seawater cooling systems have brought significant disruption to power generation. Following a related incident in 2025, the plant introduced enhanced monitoring and fishing strategies. This occurrence underscores the vulnerabilities faced by coastal nuclear installations amidst the challenges posed by extreme summer temperatures affecting France's nuclear output. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: The ground beneath Poland's wind turbines became nesting grounds for wild bees
item.description: In Poland, the bases of wind turbines have emerged as surprising havens for pollinators. Research highlights that these zones foster a thriving community of wild bees and a variety of plant species. The bare gravel and low maintenance create perfect nesting sites for ground-nesting bees. While butterflies opt for grasslands, both flies and grasslands flourish equally in these overlooked yet vital habitats for biodiversity on farmland. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: In 1958, 58 pigs were removed from Clipperton, helping seabirds grow to 137,000
item.description: Feral pigs introduced to Clipperton Island devastated seabird populations and land crabs. Ornithologist Kenneth Stager removed fifty-eight pigs, allowing the ecosystem to gradually recover. This removal helped the seabird colony grow from 650 to over 137,000 birds. Later, black rats arrived, impacting the island's vegetation and bird populations negatively. Clipperton's story highlights invasive species' profound ecological effects on islands. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Five years of Taliban rule: Afghan women face deepening repression

item.title: South Korea’s president proposes formal end to Korean war talks with North
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung proposed talks with North Korea to formally end the long-running Korean war, as Pyongyang deepens ties with Russia while asserting its status as an “irreversible” nuclear state. The two Koreas remain technically at war because their 1950-53 conflict, triggered by a North Korean attack, ended with an armistice rather than a peace treaty. Lee made the proposal in his speech at a ceremony marking the anniversary of Korea’s liberation from Japan’s 1910–45... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse

item.title: 'Begin discussions': South Korea's Lee Jae Myung calls for talks with North Korea
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung seeks peace talks to formally end the Korean War. He also wants to discuss North Korea's nuclear capabilities and reduce regional tensions. This proposal comes as North Korea strengthens its military ties with Russia. Annual US-South Korean military exercises are scheduled to begin soon. Lee also addressed improving relations with Japan and fostering prosperity. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI News Desk

item.title: Japan could be experiencing the dark side of the Pokémon obsession
item.description: Pokémon cards have spawned into a multi-billion-dollar unregulated industry, which a lawyer fears could be used for money laundering, and its homeland is now considering clamping down. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
